issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class Ride: the problem statement and UML require Ride to have two attributes (name: String, abbreviation: char) and a public constructor that accepts both parameters in that order. The solution implementation (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java) only provides a single-argument constructor public Ride(String name) which sets a default abbreviation. This contradicts the specification and causes a compilation/usage problem because RollerCoaster (src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java) calls super(name, abbreviation) expecting Ride to have a (String, char) constructor. This inconsistency will confuse students and can cause compilation errors in subclasses that forward both superclass attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public constructor in Ride with the signature Ride(String name, char abbreviation) that assigns both fields accordingly (and keep or optionally overload the existing single-argument constructor if desired). Ensure subclass constructors accept superclass attributes first and call super(name, abbreviation). Concretely, change src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java to include: public Ride(String name, char abbreviation) { this.name = name; this.abbreviation = abbreviation; } and update or retain any existing constructors so they remain consistent with the UML and the problem statement.
